showcase.title: TWCORE IG Integration
showcase.subtitle: Native support for Taiwan Core Implementation Guide — CQL examples directly aligned with local healthcare data standards
showcase.whatIsCqlContent: CQL (Clinical Quality Language) is a standardized language defined by HL7, specifically designed for expressing clinical knowledge and quality measure logic. It enables healthcare informaticists to write clinical decision rules and quality indicators in a readable, executable way.
showcase.whyTwcoreContent: TWCORE IG (Taiwan Core Implementation Guide) is a localized standard developed by the Ministry of Health and Welfare based on HL7 FHIR R4. It defines the structure and terminology mappings for Taiwan's healthcare data. All CQL examples in this platform conform to TWCORE specifications, ensuring interoperability with domestic healthcare systems.

what.title: What is CQL?
what.content: CQL (Clinical Quality Language) is a standardized language developed by HL7 International, specifically designed for expressing clinical decision logic and quality measure criteria. It is a high-level, human-readable language that can be compiled into ELM (Expression Logical Model) for computer execution.

why.title: Why CQL?
why.problems: Before CQL, clinical quality measures and decision rules were mostly written in natural language, causing:
why.problem1: Inconsistent interpretation of the same measure across systems
why.problem2: Inability to automatically compute quality measures
why.problem3: Difficult rule maintenance, prone to errors
why.solution: CQL solves these problems: it is standardized, executable, and maintains human readability.

relationship.title: CQL and FHIR Relationship
relationship.content: CQL is a query language built on top of the FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) data model. CQL accesses clinical data through FHIR resource types (such as Patient, Condition, Observation) and performs logical operations on this data.
relationship.fhirModel: FHIR provides the data model (describes data structure)
relationship.cqlLogic: CQL provides the query logic (describes how to operate on data)
relationship.together: Together, they form a complete clinical knowledge expression framework

applications.title: CQL Application Scenarios
applications.ecqm: Electronic Clinical Quality Measures (eCQM) — Automatically compute healthcare quality indicators
applications.cds: Clinical Decision Support (CDS) — Real-time medication alerts and diagnostic recommendations
applications.phenotyping: Electronic Phenotyping (ePhenotyping) — Identify specific patient populations from EHR data
applications.research: Clinical Research — Define inclusion/exclusion criteria for study populations

library.title: Library Declaration
library.content: Every CQL file is a library that must begin with a library declaration, followed by a reference to the FHIR data model.
library.explanation: The library declaration specifies the library name and version, while 'using' designates the data model.

valueset.title: ValueSet & Code
valueset.content: A ValueSet is a collection of medical terminology codes used to filter specific clinical concepts.
valueset.explanation: ValueSets can reference external terminology server definitions (e.g., VSAC), or directly define codes.

context.title: Context
context.content: Context defines the scope of CQL operations. The most common is the Patient context.
context.explanation: In Patient context, all queries are automatically scoped to the currently evaluated patient.

retrieve.title: Data Retrieval (Retrieve)
retrieve.content: Retrieve is CQL's core operation for querying data from a FHIR server.
retrieve.explanation: The bracket syntax [ResourceType: terminology] queries FHIR resources matching the criteria.

query.title: Query Expressions
query.content: CQL supports rich query syntax including where filters, sort ordering, and return projections.
query.explanation: Query syntax is similar to SQL but designed for clinical data, supporting date intervals, terminology matching, etc.

define.title: Definitions (Define)
define.content: Define creates named expressions that can be referenced by other definitions, forming logic chains.
define.explanation: Definitions are CQL's core building blocks — each quality measure population corresponds to a define statement.

overview.title: Taiwan Core Implementation Guide Overview
overview.content: TWCORE IG is a localized implementation guide developed by Taiwan's Ministry of Health and Welfare based on HL7 FHIR R4, defining standardized data formats, terminology systems, and interoperability rules for Taiwan's healthcare information exchange.

profiles.title: TWCORE Profiles & CQL
profiles.content: TWCORE defines multiple FHIR Profiles, each adapted for Taiwan's healthcare environment. When writing CQL, we use the resource types corresponding to these Profiles to query data.

codeSystems.title: Taiwan Code Systems
codeSystems.content: TWCORE defines several Taiwan-specific terminology systems for encoding local healthcare concepts:
codeSystems.icd10cm: ICD-10-CM-TW — Taiwan International Classification of Diseases (diagnoses)
codeSystems.nhiMed: NHI Medication — National Health Insurance drug codes
codeSystems.nhiProc: Medical Service Payment — NHI medical service payment codes

example.title: Full Example: Diabetes Care Quality Measure
example.description: The following example demonstrates how to use CQL + TWCORE IG to define a diabetes care quality measure calculating HbA1c screening completion rate.

examples.title: Interactive Examples
examples.subtitle: Click an example to view CQL code and detailed explanation

diabetes.title: Diabetes Care Quality
diabetes.description: Query diabetic patients' HbA1c test results using TWCORE Profiles to calculate control rates.
diabetes.explanation: This example demonstrates typical quality measure logic: defining population (diabetic patients), denominator (those who should be tested), numerator (patients with HbA1c < 7%). Uses LOINC code 4548-4 for HbA1c results.

hypertension.title: Hypertension Screening
hypertension.description: Query blood pressure measurements, identify patients with abnormal readings, and track medication usage.
hypertension.explanation: This example uses LOINC code 85354-9 (Blood Pressure Panel) to query BP records and compare systolic/diastolic thresholds. It also queries antihypertensive medications via MedicationRequest.

medication.title: Medication Safety Monitoring
medication.description: Monitor prescriptions, identify high-risk drug combinations and dose adjustment needs for renal impairment.
medication.explanation: This example combines MedicationRequest with Observation (eGFR) data to identify patients needing dose adjustments. Uses the NHI Medication code system.

encounter.title: Outpatient Visit Analysis
encounter.description: Analyze patient encounter records, calculate follow-up rates and ED-to-inpatient conversion ratios.
encounter.explanation: This example uses Encounter resources to query outpatient, emergency, and inpatient records, filtering by time intervals to compute visit statistics.

quickStart.title: Quick Start
quickStart.subtitle: Start your first CQL program in just five steps

step1.title: Step 1: Create an Account
step1.content: Click "Register" on the login page and fill in your username and password to create an account.

step2.title: Step 2: Meet the Editor
step2.content: After login, you'll enter the CQL Editor page. The left side is the code editor; the right side toggles between ELM output, execution results, or CQL Builder.

step3.title: Step 3: Write Your First CQL
step3.content: Type CQL code in the editor. Use auto-complete (Ctrl+Space) to insert TWCORE templates.

step4.title: Step 4: Translate & Validate
step4.content: Press Ctrl+S or click "Translate" to compile CQL to ELM and see validation results. Fix any errors and retranslate.

step5.title: Step 5: Execute Query
step5.content: Set the FHIR server URL, select a Patient ID, then click "Execute" (Ctrl+Enter). Results show computed values for each definition.

quickStart.nextStepsContent: Congratulations! You've completed your first CQL query. Next you can:
quickStart.next1: Explore CQL Builder to visually construct more complex queries
quickStart.next2: Go to Quality Measures to create your first eCQM indicator
quickStart.next3: Browse the FHIR Browser to discover available data on the server

q1.question: What does CQL stand for?
q1.explanation: CQL stands for Clinical Quality Language, developed by HL7 International.

q2.question: Which data model does CQL use to access clinical data?
q2.explanation: CQL is built on top of the FHIR (Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources) data model.

q3.question: How do you query all Condition resources in CQL?
q3.explanation: CQL uses bracket syntax [ResourceType] to query FHIR resources, e.g., [Condition] retrieves all Condition resources.

q4.question: What is the compiled intermediate format of CQL called?
q4.explanation: CQL is compiled to ELM (Expression Logical Model), a machine-executable logical model.

q5.question: Which organization developed the TWCORE IG?
q5.explanation: TWCORE IG is developed by Taiwan's Ministry of Health and Welfare based on HL7 FHIR R4.

q6.question: What does 'context Patient' do in CQL?
options: Scopes queries to the currently evaluated patient
q6.explanation: 'context Patient' scopes all subsequent queries to the currently evaluated patient.

q7.question: Which terminology system is primarily used for diagnoses in Taiwan?
q7.explanation: Taiwan primarily uses ICD-10-CM-TW for diagnosis coding.

q8.question: What does the 'define' keyword do in CQL?
q8.explanation: 'define' creates named expressions that can be referenced by other definitions — CQL's core building blocks.

q9.question: What lab test does LOINC code 4548-4 correspond to?
q9.explanation: LOINC 4548-4 corresponds to Hemoglobin A1c/Hemoglobin.total in Blood (HbA1c).

q10.question: What does eCQM stand for?
q10.explanation: eCQM stands for electronic Clinical Quality Measure, using CQL for measure logic definition.
